checkedAgainst: Regression, deadline and paired month fixtures; engineering policy, not population parameters. Heap cap reuses the core profiling command; job deadlines include five minutes for dependency setup. Profile parsing is bounded separately from retained summaries. Measured span: a whole year of the two-level world with the economy (audit 4, Oct 12), not a month of the full population.
semiSpaceReason: V8 young-generation size for the play server and every guarded run (core-year-speed-remaining, Oct 15): a played year allocates a great many short-lived records, and the default 16 MiB young generation spends about 16% of the year collecting. Measured on a 4-core cloud container, one process at a time, same cash to the cent: Garden City, Idaho (seed speed-gc-1) 118.5 s to 101.7 s; Exeter, New Hampshire (seed speed-ex-1) 134.3 s to 116.5 s at 64 MiB, 128.1 s at 32 MiB and 118.9 s at 128 MiB. Keep desktop/play-api-client.mjs in step.
memoryCeilingsReason: MEMORY-FLAT (docs/packages/MEMORY-FLAT.md): a two-level played world should cost tens of megabytes, as The Political Process keeps statistics per place and compact records per official. Heap after a forced collection, bookkeeping off: after importing the engine (before any town), after the opening, and growth a month from the end of the first month (whose one-time tables are excluded) to the end of the run. Starting numbers set by the package; TUNABLE against the played-world test's measured towns.
goldenBudgetReason: Measured on a four-core container: the played-world year (M0-13) takes 168 s alone and about 6 minutes on GitHub's runner, so it runs as its own job under longRunningMilliseconds. The other eleven accepted specs took 1.3, 0.4, 37.9, 35.4, 35.1, 34.6, 58.5, 36.3 and 39.8 s and two more near 35 s, about 380 s together.
timeBudgetReason: A large drawn town's year can take five to six minutes a run on GitHub's runner (Derry, New Hampshire, drawn for PR 5871: ten runs did not fit performanceMilliseconds). Base and head now alternate; after the first measured pair another starts only while the last pair's time times runTimeMargin fits the time left, and each profile only while its last run's time times profileTimeMargin does, so a large town measures fewer pairs instead of failing on time. The margins cover the run-to-run spread of a year (a few percent) plus process start and receipt parsing.
